learning_objective: The learner will classify each of ten student comments under one of seven themes, with at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** feedback-theme-coder
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify each of ten student comments under one of seven themes, with at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Qualitative Feedback, Student Survey (both defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each comment the learner commits one of seven themes. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct theme column in Content. Mastery is at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. Reading the theme list is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Comments are too subjective to code. (2) A comment can belong to only one study. (3) The most vivid comment is the most common theme. **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying comments under themes is an Understand-level action that turns words into counts. Ten comments over seven themes teach the learner to read for the main point of each. **Content:** The seven themes: Unfamiliar words, Technical problem, Wanted more practice, Simulation helped, Captions or descriptions helped, Explanations helped, Other. The ten comments (all made up, names removed): | # | Comment | Correct theme | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | I did not know what "aquifer" meant. | Unfamiliar words | The student names a word they did not know. | | 2 | The quiz would not open on my tablet. | Technical problem | It describes a failure to load. | | 3 | The slider that changes the ground cover showed me where the rain goes. | Simulation helped | It credits the simulation. | | 4 | I could follow the video because of the captions. | Captions or descriptions helped | It credits the captions. | | 5 | I wanted more questions to practice before the test. | Wanted more practice | It asks for more practice. | | 6 | When I got a question wrong, the explanation told me why. | Explanations helped | It credits the explanations. | | 7 | There were too many hard words in section 3. | Unfamiliar words | It names hard words. | | 8 | I liked the pictures. | Other | It fits none of the six named themes. | | 9 | The page was slow to load. | Technical problem | It describes a loading problem. | | 10 | A worked example would have helped. | Wanted more practice | It asks for more support to practice. | **Provenance:** The comments are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The themes follow the chapter section "Qualitative Feedback". **Rules:** Each comment has exactly one correct theme. Unfamiliar words, Technical problem, and Wanted more practice have two comments each. Simulation helped, Captions or descriptions helped, Explanations helped, and Other have one each. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one comment and the seven themes. 2. The learner places the comment under a theme, and the placement is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After comment 10 the sim shows the summary with the count for each theme. **Feedback:** 10 comments in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [theme]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This comment is [theme]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 10 correct on the first attempt" and the counts per theme. At 9 or more it adds "You can turn comments into counts." Below 9 it lists the Why text of each missed comment. **Starting State:** The first comment in the shuffled order and the seven themes. The question shown is "What is this student mainly saying?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's table of themes for the pilot uses the same six named themes.
